regions.text: しかしながら我々はこれに對して考へて見なければならない點が二つある。

quote.translation: Against this, however, there are two points that we must consider.

regions.text: 先づ第一に、或る交叉點が無開心と無闘心との交叉踏の如くに見えても、その實。

quote.translation: First, it is of course true that a point of intersection which looks like a point of intersection of indifference with indifference has sometimes in reality been brought about by causal concern.

regions.text: 因果的開心によつて將來されたものである場合のあることは勿論であるが、その故にすべての交叉點が豫め開心に依存すること投網全體のすべての絲の結び目が龍頭の一點に集中するが如くに考ふべきであらうか。

quote.translation: But should we conclude from this that every point of intersection depends in advance on concern, in the way that all the knots in all the threads of a cast net converge on the single point at its crown?

regions.text: すなはちすべて然と呼はれるものは二つ成は二つ以上の原因が一響に作用して交叉點を必然約に生じてゐるのであるとか講現象の原因のつなかかを認識しさへすれば何箏の偶然はないわけであるなどと無造作に立論の出來る筈のものであらうか。

quote.translation: Can we really argue so casually that everything called chance is two or more causes acting together and necessarily producing the point of intersection, or that there is no chance whatever so long as we know the connection among the causes of phenomena?

regions.text: 偶然と考へられたものが、或る場合に實は講原因の必然前結合から生じたものであるといふ特殊の場合を無造作に一般化してすべての偶然は諸原因の必然結合の産物であると推論するところに却つて認識の不足または思惟の幼雅がありはしないであらうか。

quote.translation: When the special case, in which what was taken for chance in fact arose from a necessary conjunction of causes, is casually generalised into the inference that all chance is the product of the necessary conjunction of causes, is it not precisely here that we find an insufficiency of knowledge, or an immaturity of thought?

regions.text: 我々は全然獨立する系列と系列とが交叉勤に於て交父する場合もあり待ることを考へて見なければならない。

quote.translation: We must consider that there can also be cases in which wholly independent series cross at a point of intersection.

regions.text: クールノ1は偶然といふ語は獨自の密度を有つた親念に對應するものであらうかその

quote.translation: Cournot asks whether the word chance corresponds to an idea with a density of its own, whether that idea has an object outside us and consequences that we cannot escape, or whether it is rather no more than a "breath of the voice" (flatus vocis), a deception to dress up our ignorance of the true causes.
